environment.description: Same application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB. Secrets are injected via AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured through a Lambda rotator (rotation interval: 60 seconds via custom RotationSchedule). The ECS task definition references secrets as valueFrom ARNs with AWSCURRENT staging label. A sidecar container runs a credential-refresh agent that sends SIGHUP to the main process every rotation cycle, triggering refreshCredentials(). DEBUG_MODE is not set (defaults to empty string). The ALB has no WAF attached. Network: the ECS service is in a private subnet with ALB in public subnet. Security group on ECS tasks only allows inbound from ALB security group on port 8080. Note: the template injection vulnerability itself remains fully exploitable - user input flows into template.Parse() without sanitization. However, any secrets exfiltrated via SSTI (e.g., using {{.}} to dump context or accessing environment via debug endpoint timing) become invalid within 60 seconds of rotation. The Secrets Manager rotation Lambda invalidates the previous version immediately upon rotation (PreviousVersion staging label is removed and the secret version is marked deprecated via custom post-rotation step), meaning stolen credentials cannot be used for lateral movement or data access.

config.runtime: ECS Fargate with Secrets Manager integration

secrets_rotation.staging_labels: AWSCURRENT replaced every 60s, AWSPREVIOUS immediately deprecated

config.sidecar: credential-refresh-agent sends SIGHUP on rotation events via CloudWatch Events trigger
config.env_vars_source: Secrets Manager ARN references in task definition (valueFrom)
